headline: Finland watches puppies grow up on a live stream

sources.title: Finland gripped by national broadcaster's puppies live stream (CNN)
Pentulive 2026: live puppy broadcast from Finland (Yle)
Video: Yle's popular Puppy Live returns for new season (Yle News)

chunks.text: Each year, people across Finland {{tune in}} to watch puppies sleep. Finland's [[national broadcaster]] runs a [[live stream]] called Puppy Live, 24 hours a day. The show {{came back}} for its sixth season in October 2026. This year it follows a mother dog of a [[curly-haired]] Italian [[breed]]. She [[gave birth]] to six puppies on October 10. The puppies will stay [[on camera]] until they leave for new homes in mid-December.

verbs.correct: To watch a show or broadcast
verbs.wrong: To record a show for later
verbs.why: Millions of people tune in to the big game every year. My grandparents tune in to the news at six. People across Finland tune in to watch the puppies sleep.

verbs.correct: To return after a time away
verbs.wrong: To move to a new channel
verbs.why: The show comes back every January. Our favorite food truck comes back to the park each spring. Puppy Live came back for its sixth season in October 2026.

chunks.text: The cameras are {{set up}} in the [[breeder]]'s home. The broadcaster keeps the breeder's name [[private]]. That way, the breeder can care for the puppies without being [[disturbed]]. Puppies sleep up to 20 hours a day, so not much {{goes on}}. It is a kind of [[slow TV]]. Still, viewers see [[milestones]] as the puppies {{grow up}}. They open their eyes, learn to walk and play outside for the first time.

verbs.why: Workers set up the stage before the concert. The teacher sets up a projector for the class. The cameras are set up in the breeder's home.

verbs.wrong: To cost a lot of money
verbs.why: A lot goes on at the market on Saturdays. Not much goes on in our town after dark. Puppies sleep up to 20 hours a day, so not much goes on.
Kittens grow up fast. Children grow up quickly, so parents take a lot of photos. Viewers get to see milestones as the puppies grow up.

chunks.text: Finland has fewer than 5.7 million people. But the show's web page {{racked up}} 6.5 million [[page views]] in 2025, the broadcaster says. Its [[clips]] on social media got about 20 million views. [[Early numbers]] suggest this year's puppies will be even more popular. Viewers helped name the puppies. They {{narrowed down}} a long list. The puppies were due to {{pick out}} their own names on October 24 by [[sniffing]] [[sealed envelopes]].

verbs.why: Funny videos rack up millions of views. Our team racks up points quickly in the second half. The show's web page racked up 6.5 million page views in 2025.

verbs.wrong: To put a list in order
verbs.why: We narrow down the list of baby names to three. Shoppers narrow down a long list before they buy a car. Viewers narrowed down a long list of names for the puppies.

verbs.correct: To choose one from a group
verbs.why: Kids pick out a toy at the store. She picks out a dress for the party. The puppies were due to pick out their own names by sniffing sealed envelopes.

chunks.text: In the [[far north]] of Finland, the sun does not {{come up}} for weeks. A researcher at the University of Eastern Finland calls the show a [[highlight]] of the winter months. People {{stay in}} more in late fall and winter, she says. The show can give them a [[sense of belonging]]. A professor at the University of Helsinki says watching a sleeping puppy {{calms people down}}. The reporter who started the show says it is about love and care. [[Unpleasant]] news often {{pushes aside}} those things.

verbs.why: The sun comes up at six in the summer. Farmers start work before the sun comes up. In the far north of Finland, the sun does not come up for weeks.
We stay in on rainy nights. Many people stay in when it snows. People in Finland stay in more in late fall and winter.

verbs.wrong: To make someone laugh a lot
verbs.why: Soft music calms my baby down. A warm bath calms me down after work. A professor says watching a sleeping puppy calms people down.
Many people push aside their health when they are busy. Big news stories push aside smaller ones. Unpleasant news often pushes aside love and care.

mainIdea.s: Finland's national broadcaster streams a mother dog and her newborn puppies all day and night. Many people watch, and experts say the show brings comfort in the dark winter.
mainIdea.why: People across Finland tune in to watch the puppies grow up. Experts say the calm show helps people during the long, dark months.

mainIdea.s: A Finnish TV show lets viewers adopt the puppies they see on its all-day live stream. Families from all over the country vote online, and the winners take a puppy home in December.
mainIdea.why: Close, but viewers only helped narrow down a list of names for the puppies. They do not vote to take the puppies home.

mainIdea.s: Scientists in Finland have found that pet dogs sleep longer during the cold winter months. They studied hundreds of family dogs and say most rest more when it gets dark early.
mainIdea.why: The real news is a live stream of a mother dog and her puppies. Many people tune in, and the show runs until mid-December.

lines.text: Have you heard about the puppy live stream in Finland?
The national broadcaster films a mother dog and her six puppies all day and all night. People {{tune in}} just to watch them sleep.
Just sleeping? That kind of [[melts my heart]].
Me too. The show {{came back}} in October for its sixth season.
The cameras are {{set up}} in the breeder's home. The puppies sleep most of the day, so not much {{goes on}}.
Do a lot of people really watch it?
The web page {{racked up}} 6.5 million views in 2025. That's more than the number of people in Finland.
Wow. I can picture people [[glued to the screen]] all winter.
In the far north, the sun doesn't {{come up}} for weeks, so people {{stay in}} a lot.
So the puppies are [[good company]] on those dark days.
Exactly. One expert says watching a sleeping puppy {{calms people down}}.
I believe it. A sleepy puppy video always [[makes my day]].
The reporter who started the show says it's about love and care, things bad news often {{pushes aside}}.
I like that. Can viewers do anything besides watch?
They helped {{narrow down}} names. Then the puppies were going to {{pick out}} their own by sniffing envelopes.
That's adorable. [[I'm hooked]], and I haven't even seen it yet.
